name: St. John’s Co-Cathedral
description: The 16th-century church of the Knights of St. John, with a gilded Baroque interior and two paintings by Caravaggio.

name: Fort St. Elmo
places: Fort St. Elmo and National War Museum
description: A star-shaped fort at the tip of the Valletta peninsula, besieged in 1565 and now home to the National War Museum.

name: Fort St. Angelo
description: A fortress across the Grand Harbour in Birgu, the knights’ headquarters during the Great Siege of 1565.

name: Grandmaster’s Palace
description: The palace of the grand masters of the Order of St. John, later the seat of British governors and now of Malta’s president.

name: Great Siege Monument
description: A bronze monument to the Great Siege of 1565, when the knights held Malta against an Ottoman fleet.

name: Triton Fountain
description: A fountain outside the city gate with three bronze tritons holding up a large basin, completed in 1959.

name: Lascaris War Rooms
description: Tunnels cut into the rock below the Upper Barrakka Gardens that served as the Allied war headquarters in the Second World War.

name: Parliament House
description: Malta’s parliament building beside the city gate, designed by the Italian architect Renzo Piano and opened in 2015.
